content: I want to build an app to save and manage bookmarks.

The baseline specification is ready for review.

- Spec: [spec.md](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/spec.md)
- Quality checklist: [requirements.md](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/checklists/requirements.md)
- Validation: all 16 checks passed; no unresolved clarifications
- Scope: personal, single-user bookmark manager with saving, tags, search, sorting, favorites, archiving, editing, and deletion

Accounts, sharing, browser synchronization/import, folders, metadata fetching, and bulk actions are excluded from the initial release.

Please approve the specification or describe any changes. Once approved, I’ll create the implementation plan; no code has been written yet.

Thanks for putting this together — I read through it carefully, and it's close on a lot of things I care about. But there are a few spots where it doesn't match what I have in my head, and I'd want those sorted before I sign off.

1. **Filling in the title for me.** I saw that automatically grabbing info about a page is listed as out of scope. That's actually one of the main things I want. When I paste in a link, I'd expect the app to go grab the page's title (and ideally a little icon or preview picture) so I don't have to type it all in myself. Having to hand-type a title for every link would make saving a chore. I'd also want to be able to tweak that fetched title before and after saving. Please pull this back into scope.

2. **When I save something I already saved.** Right now it says the app would warn me and let me save another copy. I don't want a second copy — if I try to save a link I've already got, I'd want it to just take me to the existing one so I can edit it. No duplicates sitting in my list.

3. **Searching.** The basic search is fine as a start, but I'd want a bit more. I'd like to search by a tag directly (something like typing the tag with a "#"), and to combine words — like "find this OR that" or "this but NOT that" — and to search for an exact phrase when I put it in quotes. Being able to narrow things down that way matters once I've got a lot saved.

4. **A "read later" pile.** I see favorites, which is nice, but that's not quite the same as marking something to read later. I'd want to flag things as unread/to-read and have a separate view showing just those, and mark them read once I've gotten to them.

5. **Notes.** Small one — I'd like my notes to allow a little formatting (headings, links, lists) rather than being strictly plain text, and to see them rendered nicely when I look at a bookmark.

The rest — the list view, tags, sorting, favorites, archive-vs-delete, editing, the empty states, keeping everything across sessions — all reads the way I'd expect. Could you revise around those points and show me again?

The revised specification now incorporates all five requested changes:

- Automatic title retrieval plus available site icon/preview, with editable titles and manual fallback
- Duplicate links open the existing bookmark for editing; no duplicate is created
- Advanced search supports `#tag`, quoted phrases, `OR`, `NOT`, and implicit `AND`
- A read-later queue with independent read/unread and favorite states
- Formatted notes supporting headings, links, and ordered/unordered lists

This looks great — you captured all five of the things I was worried about, and reading it back it matches what I pictured.

content:
The implementation plan is ready for review. No tasks or application code have been created yet.

Key choices:

- TypeScript across a React 19/Vite client and Express 5 server
- SQLite persistence for the single-user, 10,000-bookmark scope
- Server-side metadata retrieval with SSRF, redirect, timeout, and response-size protections
- Locally cached preview imagery rather than third-party hotlinking
- A defined search grammar that leaves parentheses/grouping for a future version
- Constrained, safely rendered Markdown for formatted notes
- Unit, integration, contract, accessibility, performance, and Playwright end-to-end testing

React’s current guidance supports Vite for scratch-built apps, while Express 5 supports the selected Node runtime: [React guidance](https://react.dev/learn/build-a-react-app-from-scratch), [Express 5 guidance](https://expressjs.com/en/guide/migrating-5/).

Artifacts:

- [Implementation plan](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/plan.md)
- [Technical research](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/research.md)

I tried the app out, and most of it behaves the way we agreed — saving works, duplicates get caught and send me back to the existing one, and favorites and read-later are separate switches. But I hit something that really worries me, and I need it fixed before I can sign off.

When I take a bookmark that has a note and tags on it, and then just flip it into my "read later" list (or mark it as a favorite), the note and all its tags disappear. I did exactly that — saved a link with a note and a tag, then toggled "read later," and afterward the note was blank and the tag was gone. I didn't touch the note or the tags; I only pressed the read-later button.

That's a real problem for me. Marking something to read later is one of the quickest, most casual things I'll do, and I'd never expect it to quietly wipe out the notes I wrote and the tags I filed it under. Same when I favorite something. Those bits of information are the whole point of keeping the bookmark — losing them is worse than not having the feature at all.

Could you fix it so that flipping the read-later or favorite switch leaves everything else on the bookmark — the note, the tags, the title — exactly as it was? Once that's sorted I'll happily take another look.

content:
Fixed and redeployed at **http://maker:4000/**.

Cause: the partial-update validator was incorrectly applying new-bookmark defaults to omitted fields. A read-later or favorite toggle therefore supplied an empty note and tag list.

State-only changes now preserve:

- Title and URL
- Formatted note
- All tags
- Favorite/read-later state not being changed
- Archive and saved media data

Regression coverage now checks read-later, favorite, read/unread, and archive toggles at both API and browser levels.

Validation:

- 53 automated tests passed
- 5 Chromium journeys passed
- Direct runtime checks confirmed the note, tags, and title survive both toggles
- Review data was reset to a clean state

The fix is in [bookmark.ts](/work/shared/src/schemas/bookmark.ts), with regression coverage in [read-later.test.ts](/work/server/tests/contract/read-later.test.ts).

That did it. I went back through the things that matter to me and they all hold up now:

- Adding something to "read later" or marking it a favorite keeps my note, my tags, and the title intact — that was my worry, and it's genuinely fixed.
- Favorites and read-later stay independent of each other.
- Searching by a tag, by an exact phrase in quotes, and excluding things with "NOT" all return what I'd expect.
- Archiving tucks a bookmark out of my main list while keeping its note and everything else, restoring brings it back, and deleting is there when I really want it gone.
- Saving, catching duplicates and sending me to the existing one — all still working.

This is the bookmark app I asked for, and it behaves the way I pictured. I'm happy to accept it. As we already agreed, grouping parts of a search together (the parentheses idea) is something I'd like to revisit in a future round, but that was intentionally left out of this version and isn't holding anything up.

Thank you — nicely done.
